- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for next 3–5 periods.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.1) and price is trending up, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to account for mean reversion bias.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.1–0.3) and price is volatile, model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values.
- If true outcome is consistently below forecast (e.g., 3+ consecutive days), model exhibits “overconfident” bias; reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 2–3 periods.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture long-term mean reversion; if sentiment is weak or neutral, forecast should align with 18-day moving average.
